newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukrainian oil terminal plans in financing woes.
newsitem.headline: Ukrainian oil terminal plans in financing woes.

text.p: Ukraine wants to build a $25 million crude oil terminal south of Odessa with an annual capacity of six million tonnes (roughly 120,000 barrels per day), but some officials have cast doubt on the project, a top regional administration official said on Monday.
"We want this terminal to provide storage for a number of (Ukrainian) regions in the south," said Vasyl Kotinkov, chief of the industry and energy department in the Kherson region.
"We are counting on private investors, including western investors, to take part in financing this project."

The terminal, to be built at the city of Kherson near the mouth of the Dnieper River on the Black Sea, has already drawn fire from officials in charge of the unfinished Odessa terminal, about 120 km (80 miles) north.

"The whole thing would require money that Ukraine doesn't have," said Anatoly Zozulya, an official in charge of oil sector investment. "We've seen Kherson's plans and they will face big problems in trying to bring in big, heavy tankers for loading."
Kotinkov said the estuary at the mouth of the Dnieper could only handle tankers with a 7,000-tonne deadweight.
"We have to deepen the estuary to allow for tankers with a 50,000-tonne deadweight," he said. "We understand that this can be very expensive."

Kotinkov said the new terminal would handle oil refined at the Kherson refinery, which has an annual capacity of 7.2 million tonnes (144,000 bpd) but which will refine only 1.5 million tonnes (30,000 bpd) this year.

Ukraine's six refineries processed up to 60 million tonnes (1.2 million bpd) of crude oil a year in the Soviet era but last year refined only 16.8 million tonnes 336,000 bpd), reflecting sharp declines in Russian oil supplies.
Construction of the Odessa terminal, with a planned capacity of 12 million tonnes (240,000 bpd) a year, has nearly ground to a halt due to financing problems.
"Ukraine doesn't have the money to complete its Odessa oil terminal, which has taken up nearly $15 million already," Zozulya said.
But he said Ukraine was seeking funding from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) to complete the $30 million project.
The Odessa project, begun in 1994, was meant to free Ukraine from dependence on Russian oil supplies by storing oil brought in from the Middle East.
